National Assembly
Twenty-first session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
22 Ashadh, 2083
Monday
Meeting No. - 27
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 12:21 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly (12:21 PM) begin. Honourable members, I have allocated one minute each for those who wish to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.

Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, I would like to express my views. I seek permission to present my views. Today, I want to speak about the statement made by the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chairperson at an election rally. He said, "Here, take it, my SIM card is also here, my SIM card will be activated. If we form a government, within 100 days, at least initially, we will paste stickers in the alleys of foreign countries for 100 youths on a free ticket. Within 100 days, we will provide the same services and facilities in this country to capable people stranded abroad as they would get abroad." I myself will go to the alleys of Australia, the alleys of Europe, the alleys of America to paste posters, calling it a golden opportunity to return to this country. Honourable Chairperson, the government has completed 100 days, but I have not seen anywhere the announced work done by the government in 100 days. Through you, Honourable Chairperson, I ask how many stickers were pasted as the Chairperson had spoken. (Time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.

Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the Balen government has deceived the Dalit community, the general public of Nepal, and the House. On Chaitra 13, when the Balen government was formed, in the fifth point of the 100-point governance reform program presented, it was announced that the Balen government would apologize to the Dalit community and bring reform programs within 15 days. Today, Ashadh 20, the current government, as mentioned in its 100-day progress report, states that it has formally acknowledged the discrimination against the Dalit and historically marginalized communities. Through you, Honourable Chairperson, I want to ask the Balen government, when did the formal apology to the Dalit community, that acknowledgment, happen? The Nepali public needs to be informed, and I also want to challenge the Balen government. The Dalits are closely watching your deception. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Manrupa Sharma.

Honourable Ms. Manrupa Sharma (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, there is talk about this blue bus. It is said that by painting the shared bus blue, facilities have been provided to women. Mothers and sons also travel, and husbands and wives also travel. When they travel together, what arrangements will be made for those mothers and sons, husbands and sons? The government is doing many good things, perhaps the only thing left for the government to do is to turn people's blood blue. I think this is the work left to be done. I want to know, is the shared bus owned by the Government of Nepal or the RSP party? Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.

Honourable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, today is Ashadh 22, the day when, in 1998 BS, 68 people, led by the scholar Yogmaya Neupane, who advocated for social justice against the oppression of the Rana regime, gender inequality, caste discrimination, and labor exploitation, took Jal Samadhi (self-immolation in water) in the Arun River at Majhuwabesi, Bhojpur. Remembering that day, I express my heartfelt tribute to them and urge the Government of Nepal, through you, Honourable Chairperson, to declare today as National Citizen Campaign Day. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Renu Chand.

Honourable Ms. Renu Chand (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, 19 people were injured in a bus accident in Gairagaon, Baitadi district. I wish the injured a speedy recovery. I demand from the government to arrange for their medical treatment and compensation. Road travel has become risky. What plans does the government have in this regard? I demand that this be presented to the House. Today is the day when scholar Yogmaya Neupane and 68 others took Jal Samadhi; I express my heartfelt tribute to them. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.

Honourable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, I want to extend my heartfelt congratulations to the government on completing 100 days. At the same time, I also want to ask, where has the announcement of the blue bus for women within the government's 100 days reached? I want to say this too, do not consider women so weak, government. Don't make it free, make it paid, but provide work. Provide respectful support, not charity. We don't need a separate bus; we can travel on shared buses too. We are not weak. Women have sent remittances to the government by sweating in foreign lands, leaving behind infants; if you can, the government should provide work to do in the country, speak the truth, not false assurances, provide work to do. Thank you, Jai Nepal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.

Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, I want to advise the government to think and consider its situation before making decisions. Hasty decisions have caused problems for the public. The demolition of the houses of the landless due to hasty decisions has now created the most complex problem. Although the government should be aware of this problem, it seems that the government, traveling in an express train, cannot hear or see. Another problem is coming. Traffic rules are being strictly enforced, and the public is starting to suffer. The government should be aware of the condition of our roads. During the rainy season, it might be easier to cross a river than to cross the road; it is becoming difficult. The potholes make the roads unsafe. In such a situation... (Time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.

Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, it has been almost a week since the Hyace vehicle accident occurred while traveling from Surkhet to Kalikot. The Government of Nepal still has not been able to determine how many people were on that vehicle. It is a far cry to find, manage, and rescue the missing members from that vehicle. From Surkhet to that place, there are police checkpoints at half a dozen places where checks are conducted. Yet, it has not been determined how many people were on that vehicle; why is the government so helpless? Can the government not even determine that, when police are deployed at various places and that vehicle is checked, on one hand? On the other hand, what is it? The government's weakness is evident in not uncovering this incident. Immediately... (Time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari.

Honourable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the landless are on the streets demanding land rights and citizenship. The government, which should be responsible for food, shelter, and clothing, has instead snatched the livelihood of disabled citizens from the streets. Farmers are wandering in search of fertilizer. With the rise in inflation, it is difficult for the general public to make ends meet. Where is the government in effective market monitoring? The problems of loan sharks and cooperative victims remain unresolved. Road accidents are increasing daily, causing significant loss of life and property. With the beginning of the monsoon, there is a high risk of floods and inundation everywhere. What is being done for disaster management response? The government is indulging in self-admiration for 87% unproductive work in 100 days, playing the drum of futility. I demand that the government provide clear answers to these numerous questions. Thank you, greetings.

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Savitri Malla.

Honourable Ms. Savitri Malla (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the Karnali Highway has become a death trap. The Prime Minister had gone to Karnali and said, "This is a dream, I will listen to Karnali." This is the reality of Karnali, Honourable Prime Minister. On Ashadh 18, a Force vehicle (Province 02-001-Kha-155) traveling from Surkhet towards Kalikot fell about 400 meters down the Syade Tola area of the Karnali Highway in Chamunda Bindrasaini Municipality-7, Dailekh district, and submerged in the Karnali River. Even after 5 days today, the vehicle's whereabouts are unknown. The bodies of 4 people have been found: driver Tularam Subedi, district Dailekh, Patpuri Municipality-8, Majhigaun, co-driver Ramprasad Subedi, district Surkhet, Patpuri Municipality-8, Majhigaun, Sirjana Khadka, district Kalikot, Raskot Municipality-2... (Time expired.)

Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable members, the order of speaking in the Zero Hour concludes here. Honourable members, I would like to inform you that the ministers concerned will respond to the questions raised during the discussion on the Appropriation Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives, under the appropriation headings. Accordingly, today, discussions related to appropriation headings of the Ministry of Youth, Labour, Employment and Social Security; Ministry of Information and Communications; Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation; Ministry of Education and Sports; Ministry of Health and Population; Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation; Ministry of Women, Children, Youth and Senior Citizens and Social Security; Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation; and Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs have been scheduled for discussion, and the concerned ministers will respond to the questions raised during the discussions on the appropriation headings related to these ministries. Honourable members, the process of the concerned ministers responding to the questions raised during the discussions on the appropriation headings related to the said ministries will now commence. Honourable members who participated in the discussion on the appropriation headings of the concerned ministry under the Appropriation Bill will be the only ones eligible to seek clarification regarding the response of the concerned Honourable Minister. Honourable members, I now provide time to the Honourable Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Ramji Yadav, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment. Honourable Minister of Youth, Labour and Employment, Mr. Ramji Yadav: Thank you. Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the issues raised by the Honourable Members are extremely important and sensitive. The ministry has prioritized internal employment creation and promotion with the intention of creating and promoting internal employment. The government has declared the decade starting from 2083...

It has been declared as the Decade of Employment Promotion. The draft of the National Employment Policy, 2083 is being prepared to make the National Employment Policy, 2071 time-appropriate. Also, the process of formulating a policy related to the care economy has been initiated for the first time in the country. Labor rights, decent work, and worker safety are not just legal commitments; these rights are being effectively implemented at the workplace. The labor inspection system is being strategically advanced with priority. In these 100 days alone, labor inspections of 1,321 establishments have been completed. Based on complaints or cases filed by workers, or during inspections, Rs. 44,096,205 has been collected as fines or settlements for issues related to labor exploitation. As a result, the inspection rate has increased significantly by 60 percent compared to the previous 9 months. Also, with the idea that responsible employers should be identified, honored, and encouraged, the ministry recently honored excellent employers for complying with labor laws. While regulating the labor sector, we have adopted both the carrot and stick approach, i.e., action and encouragement. Honorable Chairperson, honorable members have raised important questions about the budget. In the ministry's current fiscal year's annual program, budget has been allocated for employment, skill development, and entrepreneurship promotion. We have arranged for training in areas with growing demand in the labor market, such as National Apprenticeship Program based on the concept of 'earn while you learn' to get maximum results from limited resources, Career Udan programs, AI, Business Development, EV Repair, various trades in the construction sector, and the care economy, through the National Vocational Training Institute. Short-term skill training in partnership with Kathmandu University and IT, innovation, and business incubation programs have been initiated. Considering the situation where the budget allocated in previous fiscal years could not be spent, if the current budget is insufficient, more budget will be requested. I also want to clarify that the investment in the youth and employment sector is not limited to this ministry's budget alone. Programs related to youth empowerment, skills, entrepreneurship, and employment are also being conducted through various ministries and bodies such as Education, Industry, Agriculture, Information Technology, Sports, and Urban Development, Tourism, etc. This ministry has the leadership responsibility to connect, coordinate, and align these efforts according to national priorities. The Prime Minister's Employment Program initially progressed as a social protection-oriented program to provide minimum employment opportunities to unemployed citizens. Now, through the National Employment Program, we do not want to remain limited to short-term employment. We want to connect this program with skills and entrepreneurship. The foundation for advancing employment, skill development, labor market information, entrepreneurship counseling, and employment missions through a single system has now been prepared through the National Employment Program. Our main goal is to connect the skills, experience, and entrepreneurship of returning migrants with national construction. The Retained Management Information System for integrated data of individuals returning with skills and experience from abroad is in the testing phase. Through the REMI project, operated in 20 local levels and two provinces of Koshi and Madhesh, orientation and counseling services have been provided to 20,154 returning migrant workers and their family members. 1,086 returning workers have obtained employment or self-employment opportunities, while 936 have built the foundation for entrepreneurship by preparing business plans with the support of local and provincial governments. 305 returning migrant worker cooperatives have been formed at local to provincial levels, expanding community support and access. As you may be aware, various complaints are being received regarding foreign employment seekers not receiving the work and salary as per their contracts. It is the ministry's responsibility to carry out rescue operations in such cases. In this regard, by resolving 1,004 cases of fraud related to foreign employment, both individual and institutional, compensation of approximately Rs. 307,500,000 has been recovered for citizens. While compensation of Rs. 126,700,000 was provided to victims of foreign employment in the 9 months before the government was formed, more than Rs. 300,000,000 in compensation has been disbursed within the 100 days of the government's formation. On a monthly average basis, the rate of compensation disbursement has increased by approximately 628 percent. Similarly, 11,528 case files related to foreign employment since the year 2057 BS have been digitized. The web portal uur.doj.gov.np has also been prepared for digitizing and tracking issues related to employment, research, and compensation for foreign employment services. An Action Command Center has been operationalized at the ministry level to promptly address complaints and fraud incidents related to foreign employment, and Operation Illegal Agent Cleanup web portal has been launched and initiated as a national campaign. A mobile app related to this is in the construction phase. Honorable members, we have not encouraged foreign employment; we have managed it to the maximum extent. Honorable Chairperson, social security is a major priority of the government. A policy to bring workers in the informal sector, self-employed, and those in foreign employment under the umbrella of social security has been advanced. Finally, I would like to thank all the honorable members once again for the important questions, suggestions, and advice they have raised. Creating an environment for decent work for Nepali youth in Nepal and making foreign employment safe, organized, and dignified is our common priority. The ministry is working on a war footing for this task. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, I will provide time to honorable members who wish to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Youth, Labor, and Employment, Ramji Yadav. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that no honorable member has requested time to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Youth, Labor, and Employment, Ramji Yadav, on the appropriation title related to the Appropriation Bill, 2083, concerning the Ministry of Youth, Labor, and Employment. Honorable members, the discussion on the appropriation title related to the Ministry of Youth, Labor, and Employment concludes here. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Vikram Timilsina, to respond to the questions raised on the appropriation titles related to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Honorable Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Vikram Timilsina: - Honorable Chairperson, I am present to respond to the questions raised in the discussion on various titles under the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology within the Appropriation Bill, 2083. First of all, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the honorable members who have studied and asked questions regarding the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Before going to the questions, I would like to express my sincere thanks to the Honorable Chairperson for this opportunity, and I would like to inform all honorable members through the Honorable Chairperson that if there are any problems related to the communications and information technology sector, or if there are any questions, they can be raised by coming to the ministry, and the ministry will take steps to resolve the problems. And I would like to go directly to the questions. As far as I know, only one question has been raised related to the ministry. Honorable Roshni Mechhe has asked two specific questions. Her question is why the government's priority is to purchase such vehicles and machines, such as a mobile frequency monitoring van for Rs. 15 crore and a secure printing press machine for Rs. 22 crore, under the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology in the budget for the fiscal year 2083/084, when students in remote areas are not receiving notebooks and textbooks. Honorable members have drawn attention to the sensitive situation where students in remote areas are not even receiving notebooks and textbooks. This issue is itself valid and serious. However, the matter of allocating Rs. 15 crore for the purchase of a mobile frequency monitoring van and Rs. 22 crore for the purchase of a secure printing press under the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology in the budget for the fiscal year 2083/084, and the need for educational materials are not alternatives to each other. One does not preclude the other. These are different titles, different natures, different objectives, and subjects that different ministries of the government need to look into. First of all, I would like to clarify why the budget has been allocated for the process of purchasing a mobile frequency monitoring van. A mobile frequency monitoring van is not just a vehicle. It is a mobile laboratory for radio spectrum monitoring, a mobile spectrum monitoring laboratory. Since radio frequency spectrum, i.e., electromagnetic waves, cannot be seen with the naked eye, touched, or felt, a radio frequency monitoring system is required for its monitoring. As per the recommendations of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), the installation and operation of a radio frequency monitoring system in Nepal are mandatory, and this system requires very large resources. A radio frequency monitoring system that can reach across the country has not been established to date, and a significant amount of resources is immediately required for its operation, making it seem impossible. In this context, it is essential to install, purchase, and operate a radio frequency monitoring system installed in a mobile van and monitor it by taking it to various locations as needed. Since installing that monitoring system in various places would cost billions, it is being done by placing that equipment in a mobile van and taking it to various places for monitoring as needed. The radio frequency monitoring system contributes significantly to the effective management of the limited natural resource of the frequency spectrum, identification of illegal telecommunication systems, FM stations, wireless systems, and other radio equipment operating without a license, intervention with licensed institutions and individuals, control of frequency interference, determination of cross-border frequency interference in border areas, effective implementation of standards and spectrum management responsibilities related to the International Telecommunication Union, effective regulation and monitoring of modern wireless services such as 4G, 5G, digital broadcasting, IoT, improvement of the quality of telecommunication and broadcasting services, bringing the use of unlicensed frequency and illegal equipment under the purview of regulation and increasing revenue through license and spectrum fees, identification of suspicious or unauthorized radio communication in sensitive areas. In the long term, it ensures the transparent, secure, and efficient use of limited national resources like the radio spectrum and provides economic, technical, and institutional benefits to the nation.

Directly from effective management and monitoring of the frequency spectrum, the government receives an annual revenue of approximately 4.15 billion rupees from frequency and spectrum, and indirectly contributes about 1.5 percent of GDP. In this context, this mobile monitoring van has been purchased, including equipment. For the past nearly 7 years, due to the absence of that van, the van being broken, and the inability to utilize the service, there have been problems. When work had to be done using vans borrowed from other government agencies, difficulties arose. Therefore, the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology allocated a budget and paved the way for this van. The goal is to increase revenue from licenses and spectrum fees by bringing the use of unlicensed frequency and illegal equipment under regulatory scope. This is a kind of investment, not just an expense. It was also essential for identifying and resolving harmful interference caused by unauthorized use of radio frequency and use contrary to technical standards. In the past, the mobile frequency monitoring van purchased in 2001 with loan investment from the World Bank under the Telecommunications Sector Reform Project was inoperable. The annual maintenance and upgrade costs were very high, appearing to be more than the cost of buying a new one. Therefore, to purchase a new mobile frequency monitoring van with higher capacity in a high-frequency range than the capacity of the old mobile frequency monitoring van, which was necessary and cost-effective, a budget has been arranged for the purchase and operation of a mobile frequency monitoring van. Second, regarding the Security Printing Press. There was a question about the justification for allocating 220 million for the Security Printing Press machine. Although before this, not millions but billions worth of equipment under the Security Printing Center were purchased, and it is difficult to answer why they were purchased, we have had to bear the burden of those issues today. Some of those issues are in court, some are with the Commission for Investigation of Abuse of Authority. The situation is very dire. If we look at that scenario, questions have arisen as to why such large equipment worth billions and buildings worth millions were built. However, there is a clear reason why we are about to purchase this printing machine worth 220 million. I want to provide that reason and inform you, through the Chairperson, that I will be present in the next session to provide clarity on how it has been used and how no irregularities have occurred. According to the Security Printing Act, 2081, the Security Printing Center is the sole responsible body for printing and producing national security documents. In the current fiscal year, the center has printed 2.4 million smart driving licenses so far, relieving citizens of the problems they previously faced. It has printed 3.5 million postage stamps and other documents and handed them over to the concerned bodies. In the next fiscal year, it is a mandatory obligation stipulated by law that other security documents to be added within the center's scope of work, such as excise duty stamps, citizenship certificates, and national identity cards, must be produced through the center. This is not a voluntary expense. It is impossible to fulfill the production obligations stipulated by law without the necessary equipment. Currently, the Security Printing Center has machines for printing paper-based materials. However, this is being done because there are no machines for printing card-based materials. This is not a consumption expense; it is a capital investment that yields returns. The 220 million is not a current consumption expense; it is a capital investment in an income-generating asset. Since the Security Printing Center is a commercially operated entity, this machine will replace printing currently done abroad with domestic production, saving foreign currency. It will generate revenue through printing services and return it to the state treasury, and will recoup the investment within its useful life. In other words, this investment is self-sustaining; it does not deplete resources but creates them, which can also be used for education and other priorities. With the implementation of the Act, the center's production capacity and output will increase next year. The current printing capacity will not be able to meet this growing demand. If machines are not added, the obligation to have legally mandated production done abroad at higher costs and with security risks will continue. This capital investment, which aims to make the Security Printing Center self-reliant and profitable, will strengthen the state's long-term financial capacity and increase the state's ability to invest in social priorities like education. For this reason, I want to inform the honorable members that the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology has thoughtfully considered the purchase of these two items – one machine and another monitoring van. I also want to inform you that this year, I have personally sat down and discussed the budget for every item under this ministry. The budget, which comes from the sweat of the people, has been allocated and spent in the correct areas, with any excess being minimized. I also want to express my belief that in the coming days, any questions, suggestions, advice, and various issues that have reached us concerning this ministry will be brought to us, and we will cooperate in addressing them. Thank you, Namaste. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I will now provide time to honorable members who wish to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Vikram Timilsena. (12:46 PM) Each honorable member wishing to seek clarification will be allocated 1 minute. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that no names have been received from any honorable members to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Communications and Information Technology, Dr. Vikram Timilsena, on the appropriation bill, 2083, under the heading related to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology. Honorable members, the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology concludes here. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Khadga Bahadur Paudel, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation. (12:58 PM) Honorable Minister of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, Mr. Khadga Bahadur Paudel: Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, Respected Questioners, I wish to enter into the subjects related to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation raised during the discussion on the Appropriation Bill, 2083/084, in the National Assembly on Ashadh 18, 2083, and the related queries. Today, as I have a role in both houses, I had to come in a hurry, but I have arrived on time. First, I would like to address the question raised by the Honorable Bishnu Devi Pudasaini. She raised the point that Kathmandu is a city that receives many guests, and no ministry seemed to have addressed this. She questioned why, despite the need to beautify Kathmandu, including the Bagmati River flowing through the heart of Kathmandu, which is mixed with sewage, and the rivers, monasteries, deities, and sacred land, no budget was visible. She also mentioned that while it seemed there was some knowledge about heritage, it didn't appear that heritage was being cherished. She stated that millions of people come to visit Pashupatinath, but the name Pashupatinath was not mentioned anywhere in the budget. She also expressed happiness that some funds were allocated to Gokarna Palace and that it was her view to develop the area of the historical figure Sundarijal as an important tourist destination. Now, I would like to address the honorable member's question and query. Various bodies, including the Department of Archaeology and various museums, are operating under the ministry. Cultural promotion programs are in operation, and budgets have also been allocated for various programs. In the policy program and budget, we are continuously working for heritage conservation and promotion. Regarding the budget for the Pashupatinath area, the main point is that the Pashupati Area Development Trust generates its own budget and does not receive it from elsewhere, which I would also like to inform the honorable house. We have allocated 382.4 million rupees for cultural promotion, 484.4 million rupees through the Department of Archaeology, and 105 million rupees through the Buddhist Philosophy and Monastery Development Committee, totaling an allocation of 971.9 million rupees. I would also like to address the query of the Honorable Jayanti Devi Rai. She stated that the tourism sector contributes to the country's economy and that attention needs to be paid to tourism promotion. There are important places in remote areas, but they do not seem to have been addressed. She complained that the plans she had put forward did not receive budget allocation and also complained that plans listed in the national heritage list were overlooked. Honorable member, the Ministry of Tourism is continuously active in preserving and promoting culture, developing the tourism sector, and developing and expanding civil aviation. The ministry has attempted to allocate the budget equitably across the country within the allocated budget limit and ceiling. Given the high demand for budget and the demands of many honorable members, we have calculated that our ministry requires approximately 1 trillion 63 billion rupees to address that budget. This is an extremely large amount. Nevertheless, I would like to inform you that budgets have been allocated for various places requested by the honorable member, including Bhojpur and various other places like Mundum Trail. I would also like to address the query raised by the Honorable Sonam Geljen Sherpa. He used a symbolic comparison between Singha Durbar and the Himalayas. He explained that just as the Himalayas look beautiful from afar but are cold deserts up close, Singha Durbar was also explained as a type of cold desert. He also expressed concern that the pressure on Mount Everest has increased, with data showing over 1004, or rather over 1008 people, climbing the mountain at that time. He expressed concern that if the exploitation of the Himalayas continues to increase, Mount Everest will not remain intact. I agree with his concern. For that purpose, in the regulations and procedures that are currently being developed for the tourism act, we are going to include a provision that one cannot climb Everest without climbing a peak above 7000 meters. This is primarily about increasing the royalty for the Himalayas and is essentially a matter for the Ministry of Finance in terms of non-tax revenue. However, in coordination with the Ministry of Finance, we are committed to reducing the pressure on Everest in the coming days. I would like to state this. He also alluded to the fact that the ministry is focusing on health tourism or other tourism issues, suggesting that the Himalayas are our main ripe fruit, and we should not stray from them. We need to consider the diversity of tourism. Promoting tourism in only one sector and relying solely on that...

If it is based on that, then it cannot be sustainable. For that, we have brought such plans saying that we will enter into various dimensions of tourism. Along with that, he had raised the issue that the government should work towards the conservation of Twin Otter aircraft and also pointed out that the number of Twin Otter aircraft is decreasing and flights to remote hilly areas are gradually reducing. I will definitely give the necessary instructions to the Nepal Airlines Corporation to increase and conserve the number of Twin Otter aircraft, and along with that, I would like to inform you that we will also cooperate with other private airline service providers. Similarly, I would like to present the issue raised by the Honorable Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar. He had raised the issue that tourism could not be attracted as per the target and tourism activities are not progressing in an organized manner, airports are dilapidated, and existing ones are not operational. Honorable member has indeed spoken the truth. It is difficult to attract tourism as per the target. We also keep the target open, don't we? However, this season, due to various reasons, a large influx of Indian tourists, I had just returned from observing the Mustang region today, and in many places, various pilgrimage sites of Nepal, from Mechi to Mahakali, hill stations, and cold places, a very large number of Indian tourists are currently present. In the Muktinath region alone, last year during this month, we had obtained data that more than 1 lakh 32 thousand Indian tourists had entered. However, the correct data, the exact data is yet to come, we had seen such things. We have emphasized collaboration with government, private, non-governmental, donor agencies, and other diasporas in attracting and promoting tourism, and I would like to inform you that work is being done in a systematic and sustainable manner, rather than a hasty reactive approach, with a policy-oriented approach. Along with that, I will move on to the query from the Honorable Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. He had said that it would be appropriate to separate culture from tourism and place it under education, and that the budget for the tourism sector was insufficient, and that not much attention was paid to attracting tourists. Budget was allocated for Nijgadh Airport but it was not mentioned in the policy and programs. A budget was allocated for a temple in Ayodhya, India, which was not good, and he raised such issues. I would like to address that. Whether it is appropriate or not to separate culture from tourism and place it under education is actually decided according to the Nepal Government's Rules of Business, so for now, I would like to inform you that it is currently under the Ministry of Tourism. And when discussing this matter, since tourists come to study, observe, and research arts, culture, and archaeological heritage, it seems appropriate to me that it belongs under this ministry. Secondly, he stated that the budget for the tourism sector is insufficient, and that is my opinion as well. The budget is not enough, the allocation is small. It would be good if we received a little more than others. Regarding attracting tourists, I have already explained in response to the query of the Honorable Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar, so I will not go into that. This amounts to about 4.44 percent of the national budget. Investment in health is not an expense. It is for the country.

It is the most important investment in the future and human capital formation. By reducing the financial burden of citizens' healthcare and increasing production through healthy citizens, sustainable development can be achieved, necessitating adequate investment in the health sector. To implement the fundamental right to health guaranteed by the constitution, the government is committed to achieving the target of 10 percent set by the National Health Financing Strategy. Accordingly, the health budget needs to be gradually increased in the coming fiscal years and moved towards practical implementation.

Out of the total budget allocated to the Ministry, 5 billion 62 crore 51 lakh has been allocated to the federal government and 34 billion 82 crore 96 lakh as conditional grants to local levels.

Honorable Chairperson, I would now like to present my views and suggestions regarding the budget and annual program for the upcoming fiscal year of the Ministry of Health and Population.

Honorable members have raised questions regarding the mention by the Honorable Finance Minister in the budget speech for fiscal year 2083/084 that a budget of 101 billion 95 crore has been allocated to the health sector, while the budget for the Ministry of Health and Population appears to be only around 96 billion 37 crore 73 lakh. Regarding this, the 96 billion 37 crore 73 lakh is the allocated budget including grants transferred to bodies under the Ministry of Health and Population, provinces, and local levels. The 101 billion 94 crore mentioned in the budget speech is the total budget allocated to the country's overall health sector, which also includes the budgets allocated to the Civil Hospital, Police Hospital, etc. These fall under the purview of the Ministry of Health and Population but are part of the country's overall health sector.

Regarding the honorable members' question about the operation of basic health services, there is a target to construct basic hospitals in 657 local levels across the country, of which construction has been completed in 109 local levels, construction is underway in 336 local levels, and the remaining local level hospitals are planned for construction based on scientific mapping and strategic approach. The operation of basic hospitals whose construction has been completed is a shared responsibility of all three tiers of government. For this, the federal ministry has prepared standards and procedures, and arrangements have been made to provide operational expenses. In addition, investment from the provincial and local levels is also essential. Although basic health services are exclusively within the jurisdiction of local levels as per the constitution, there is a demand from local levels for specialized services like dialysis and ICU. Specialist services are not currently possible in basic hospitals. Therefore, other services should be expanded gradually only after basic health services are fully delivered. We have already allocated budget in our program for the upcoming year to prepare standards for the integrated operation of basic health service packages. I also look forward to your valuable suggestions on how this can be improved.

Honorable members have also informed about the lack of adequate budget allocation in the field of food hygiene and nutrition. Under Nepal's Third Multi-Sectoral Nutrition Plan (MSNP III), the nutrition-specific programs operated by the Ministry of Health and Population and the Department of Health Services are the backbone for reducing maternal and child malnutrition. These programs include monitoring the growth of children under 5 years, distribution of iron and folic acid to pregnant and lactating mothers, vitamin A and deworming campaigns, and provision of nutrition rehabilitation homes for the treatment of severe malnutrition. However, due to changing lifestyles and excessive consumption of junk food, the existing maternal and child-centric programs alone are not sufficient to reduce malnutrition. Therefore, recognizing the severity of malnutrition at the local and provincial levels, it is necessary to allocate more budget to these nutrition-specific programs, coordinate with sectors such as agriculture, drinking water, and sanitation, and implement nutrition-sensitive activities that address the root causes of malnutrition. For nutrition-related programs under the Family Welfare Program, a total of 73 crore 6 lakh has been allocated for fiscal year 2083/084: 13 crore 1 lakh from the federal government, 37 crore 84 lakh from the provinces, and 32 crore 20 lakh from local levels. Similarly, I would like to inform you that a budget of 48 crore 79 lakh has been allocated for the upcoming fiscal year for food, technology, and quality control.

Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my sincere gratitude for the important questions, suggestions, and concerns raised by the honorable members regarding health insurance. The main objective of health insurance is to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure on health by managing the treatment costs of the sick and the poor and helpless citizens through the contribution of healthy and capable citizens. Health insurance is not a profit-making business like other commercial insurance. It is a social health security program. Therefore, health insurance should be viewed not from a profit and loss perspective, but as social justice, risk sharing, and state investment in the health sector. This program provides financial security to citizens and also creates an important basis for strengthening health institutions. The government has given high priority to health insurance, with an allocation of 7.5 billion in the fiscal year, 10 billion in the current fiscal year, and an estimated 15 billion in the upcoming fiscal year. More than 23 billion has been paid in the current fiscal year. With this payment, all claims of service provider health institutions affiliated with the Health Insurance Board as of the end of Mangsir 2082 have been settled. I would also like to inform you that coordination and continuous efforts are underway with the relevant bodies to manage the necessary budget and ensure sustainable financial sources for claims payments after Mangsir 2082.

The main challenges of the current health insurance program are the ineffective implementation of mandatory participation of employees and organizations in the organized sector. Furthermore, the need for improvement in the insurance management system and the fact that most patients are only individuals create challenges for the sustainability of the insurance. The Ministry has taken both short-term and long-term corrective steps to improve health insurance. Short-term measures include a comprehensive review of the benefit package, management of insurance services in private health institutions, effective monitoring, strengthening of the official IT system, and improvement of service management programs. In the long term, the policy adopted is to ensure basic health services separately from the insurance program by the state, to make health insurance mandatory for all employees in the organized sector, and to create an effective social health security system by integrating health security programs operated under the Social Security Fund.

This year, we are also restructuring the curriculum and revising the entire curriculum from class 1 to 5. Institutional schools will also increase human resources and curriculum as needed.

As it is being adjusted accordingly, the results were even more visible in the past. But from this year, we will gradually develop the curriculum in community schools as well, and pay a little attention to vocational education. We are trying to duplicate what we have been practicing in Kathmandu Metropolitan City in the past, and we will gradually increase it in a systematic manner. I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Member for the question raised, and I also fully support his curiosity and the points raised. The Honorable Member has raised a question about why other communities were not included when we only included Dalits, Chamars, and Vodis in the Dalit quota for MBBS students. Regarding this, if there are other communities that should be included, we can discuss and amend the laws in collaboration and coordination with the Honorable Member, and proceed accordingly. For that, I would also like to invite the Honorable Member to the Ministry. Yes, thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Let's observe a minute of silence for a minute and a half. (15:32) We must learn. Honorable Members, the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Education and Sports concludes here. And there is one ministry left, the Minister of Law is coming, so this has been done, it is being tried to do this again, it should be discussed directly, why should it be done? Huh? He went there when it was urgent, and now he has come here. That's what I heard, that he has arrived. Okay. Honorable Members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, to respond to the questions raised in the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: (15:34) Honorable Chairperson, regarding the discussion related to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Honorable Khamma Bahadur Khati participated in the discussion on the Appropriation Bill and provided important suggestions and showed interest in making the programs and budget more effective. Therefore, through the Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Honorable Member. I believe that the suggestions, interests, and concerns of the Honorable Member will further refine and make the programs and budget allocated to the Ministry more effective. Basically, the issues raised by the Honorable Member include the need to complete legal reforms within the deadline, to accelerate the repeal and amendment of irrelevant laws, to effectively expand digital legal services nationwide, to effectively manage government cases, to develop the capacity of judges, and to regularly submit progress reports to the parliament. It would be good if this practice is institutionalized. Coordination and cooperation in law-making between the federal, provincial, and local levels should be done. The Ministry of Law should take the lead in ensuring that decisions of the Council of Ministers are made in accordance with the constitution and laws, and that transitional justice work is made effective. These are the issues that the Honorable Member has raised during the discussion. The Honorable Member has raised a very important issue regarding the deadline and timeliness of legal reforms. In the previous term, when I was a member of the Federal Parliament, I also raised this issue repeatedly in the House of Representatives, and at that time, my statement was very clear. The government, as it presents the budget in the upcoming fiscal year, the budget should provide an estimate of how the country's economic prosperity will be in the future. Similarly, it was my clear demand that the parliament should be informed about what laws will be introduced in the upcoming fiscal year. Accordingly, we now have the Legislation Act, 2081, and the Legislation Act, 2081 also mandates that the government must provide a list of the laws it plans to introduce in the upcoming fiscal year. Coincidentally and fortunately, I was also a member of the committee during the formulation of this Legislation Act and played a very active role in it. And now, we are almost in the final stages of preparing to provide you with a list of what laws the government is preparing to enact in the upcoming fiscal year, along with the list for the Federal Parliament. Discussions with all ministries have been completed. Lists of which laws are to be made have been received from them. Now, after setting priorities, we will present them to the Federal Parliament. I would like to request the Honorable Members. The next issue is the need to accelerate the repeal and amendment of irrelevant laws, which is a very practical issue that has been raised. We have declared the upcoming fiscal year as the year of legal reform and law-making. Therefore, the ministry is currently preparing to repeal all laws that need to be repealed in the upcoming fiscal year and to amend all new laws as part of a campaign for legal reform. We are also preparing to form a high-level committee for this. The actual announcement will be made on July 1st. Detailed information will be available on July 1st. In any case, we have studied the concerns raised by you extensively. This study has also been done in the National Assembly. There is also a report from the National Assembly on which laws need to be introduced after the promulgation of the constitution and which laws are inconsistent with the constitution. Similar studies have been conducted in many places. Our goal is to reform the laws in the coming year by considering these studies as reference material. I would also like to inform you about this. Another issue is that to emphasize digital legal services, the ministry has now introduced the Integrated Legal Aid Reporting Software System. Honorable Members may already be aware of this. The Ministry of Law has practiced this before, but it was not very effective. But I would like to inform you and give you a notice. In our Integrated Legal Aid Reporting Software System, both service providers and service recipients can request legal consultation or services they need in one place. And many lawyers may be willing to provide services, but they may not find anyone to provide them to. And many lawyers provide free legal services. There is no record of them, and the state has no record. Therefore, through this Integrated Legal Aid Reporting Software System, those who provide legal services, consultations, or litigation services can update them on the software, and those who seek legal consultation can also request the state if they need something. We have created such a system, and I would like to inform you about this. I would like to request you all to spread the word in society among your acquaintances that the government has initiated this. Similarly, the legal services provided by the District Legal Aid Officers are currently being reported to the Ministry through this software system. There are complaints that the services provided by the District Legal Aid Officers are not sufficient. We are preparing to amend the law and increase the number of these legal aid officers in the upcoming fiscal year. In any case, if we can make this system effective, and if the private sector and the government sector stand together in providing legal services, I believe that we will be able to achieve appropriate results in the right to justice of the citizens. Similarly, what we have done now is that on the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs website, there is a place to give suggestions. After clicking there, you can give suggestions throughout the year about what laws you think should be made. Ordinary citizens can also give suggestions there, and Honorable Members can also suggest what laws should be introduced. We are taking that as reference material and preparing to study it and draft bills. You can also give suggestions through that portal if you think any laws are old or if you think new laws should be introduced. Another thing we have is the Nepal Law Information System. I think our target is to complete it by October or November of the upcoming fiscal year. By the middle of the upcoming fiscal year, all the laws of the provinces, federal, and local levels. If we look for them now, they are not found anywhere, not in one place. Therefore, to keep them in one place, we are creating a system called Nepal Law Information System. We are managing all the laws of the local, provincial, and federal governments to be available on one platform. I would also like to inform the Honorable Members about this. The Honorable Member has suggested making government case management more effective. In this regard, I would like to inform you that necessary initiatives are being taken to facilitate implementation by tracking all stages from case filing to execution through a digital system. On this occasion, we also expect that Honorable Members will provide further suggestions to make the aforementioned efforts related to digital legal services by the Ministry of Law more effective. We also expect that you will play a role in bringing these mediums and services to the general public. Regarding the progress report, we inform about it from time to time in the course of giving answers and in various discussions of the committee. Our interactions indicate what is happening in the ministry and how the work is being done. The main thing is that according to the Legislation Act, 2081, the government will be informed about what laws it will make in the upcoming fiscal year, and I believe that there will be sufficient time to discuss these matters with stakeholders. I would also like to inform you that we are facilitating this by providing the list from this year onwards, and providing the list of laws for the upcoming fiscal year to prepare. The Honorable Member stated that the decisions of the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal should be in accordance with the constitution and laws.

The Ministry of Law has a leading role in this, and a very important and relevant issue has also been raised. The Government of Nepal is committed to constitutional supremacy and the rule of law. In this regard, I would like to request that the Ministry of Law is carrying out the necessary coordination and facilitation work in accordance with the cooperation as per the Government of Nepal (Allocation of Business) Rules, 2083. The honorable member has also expressed concern and interest regarding the progress of transitional justice. I would also like to state that the government is working with high priority to bring the pending transitional justice processes to a conclusion as soon as possible. The necessary budget has also been allocated for the commissions related to transitional justice, namely the Truth and Reconciliation Commission and the Commission of Investigation on Enforced Disappearances. The Government of Nepal has established a fund by making regulations for the compensation of victims, and the draft regulations for the Commission of Investigation on Enforced Disappearances, 2083 and the Truth and Reconciliation Commission Regulations, 2083 have been prepared and submitted to the Council of Ministers for approval. Similarly, the honorable member has expressed concern and interest regarding coordination and cooperation in law-making at the federal, provincial, and local levels. In this regard, the Ministry of Law studies the laws made by the provinces and local levels and submits reports to the National Coordination Council as per the Federal, Provincial, and Local Coordination and Interrelationship Act, 2077. The ministry has submitted such study reports twice before, and the study work in the current fiscal year has also been completed and the report is in the final stages of preparation. I would also like to request that the necessary process will be initiated to harmonize the laws made by all three levels based on the suggestions of the aforementioned report. Finally, I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude once again to all the honorable members who participated in the discussion on the budget appropriations of the Ministry of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, through the Honorable Chairperson, and express my commitment to making the ministry's performance effective within the allocated budget limit for the Ministry of Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs. Thank you.
